name: citymeter-shell
about: Shared code of the CityMETER demos. Navigation (0.1.0): address grammar d/at/e/n with browser history, breadcrumb, tab title. Map (0.2.0): camera presets and the building camera, terrain mode, building x-ray, building join and the CityMETER/OSM building units, vector-tile decoding, planar geometry, the basemap style, the MapLibre 5.6.2 guards and the MapLibre loader. Header (0.3.0): the launch card with one automatic retry, the nav-7 glyphs and help dialog, the dataset picker and the list of demos. Levels (0.4.0): the subdistrict (แขวง/ตำบล) and the local administrative unit (อปท.) in the address and the breadcrumb, for the demos that open them; the locale (ย่าน, 0.4.1). Zones (0.4.2): a zone a dataset defines itself stays a filter that opens a level, its crumb has no production link, and the dataset picker names the place `at` hands over. Networks (0.4.3): a network the reader came through (a rail line, a brand) gets a crumb without a production link, a dataset without a registry code writes no `d`, a link can open the help dialog at one of its sections (data-open-help), a demo can mark its own new-tab links like the shared ones, and every demo is on the shell. Same bytes in every repository that carries it, and so are the files under shared; change them everywhere at once (demo-platform-review, phase 1). Language (0.5.0): one language per page from ?lang= (production style), Thai the source; on a page that declares English (meta citymeter:languages) the page text is replaced in the DOM from dictionaries keyed by the Thai text, names only from the data's own English, Thai dates in the Christian era; the language link and the hub link (“ดูเดโมทั้งหมด”) in the header, the theme control in the list on every width. Words in context (0.5.1): a dictionary entry can depend on its element (a tile label under its number reads “77 provinces”, the filter “Province”), and from an English page the picker marks the demos that are Thai only. Cut titles and context patterns (0.5.2): a tab title cut to 60 characters still reads the name it begins with, a context entry can carry its own patterns (a number read by where it stands), a pattern can translate a longer piece with its separators (tools.text), a name that stays Thai and fills its element is marked lang="th", and School, Government Office and Factory declare English. Pharmacy and Restaurants declare English (0.5.3). Industrial Estate (0.5.4): a demo kept inside another repository (`pages` in js/shell/datasets.js: its GitHub Pages path, montri-th.github.io/factory/industrialestate/; `path` its path on the CityMETER Pages site), the picker never takes it for its host (the longest path wins), and it declares English. A result that lacks a part, and the map earlier (0.6.0): a demo that could not load one of its optional files says so (`citymeter:partial`) and the launch script shows what is missing, what that does to the result and a reload, folded to a mark that stays; the pinned MapLibre files start loading with the data and carry Subresource Integrity values (launch.js and vendors.js, kept equal by the tests); a line says the map is still loading after the data is on the page; performance marks citymeter:ready, citymeter:map-ready and citymeter:partial. Lighter massing (0.6.0): parseVectorTile reads only the layers it is asked for, and ringsIntersect keeps a ring's box and skips the edges that cannot cross. A phone and the dark theme (0.6.0, owner 2026-11-11 20:38): the launch script sets the theme before the first paint (data-theme-key, color-scheme, theme-color), keeps a mark while the page is on screen and starts the tab lean after the browser ended it or the map lost its context (`citymeter:map-trouble`, html[data-lean]), the notice is a short card on a phone and carries the lean note with a way back to the full map; maplibre-guard.js gives the map's budget by device (mapBudget, budgetPixelRatio), caps the terrain's texture pool (capTerrainPool, terrain.js `pool`) and watches for a lost context (watchContext, reloadOnContextLoss); the map's own buttons are themed in the dark theme (navigation.css).
